newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico police make arrest in slain journalist case.
newsitem.headline: Mexico police make arrest in slain journalist case.

text.p: Mexican police have arrested a man in connection with the murder of a crusading anti-drug journalist, and say a cocaine lord probably ordered the hit, La Jornada newspaper said on Saturday.

The paper said police in the northern state of Sonora had arrested Rolando Arroyo Palacios, nicknamed "Long Hair," in San Luis Rio Colorado -- the town on the Arizona border where Benjamin Flores Gonzalez was gunned down on Tuesday.
The paper quoted Sonora state attorney Rolando Tavares Ibarra as saying the killing may have been ordered by a drug lord "who was annoyed by articles in La Prensa."
La Prensa is the name of the newspaper Flores founded and directed in San Luis Rio Colorado and which published his hard-hitting reports on corruption and the drug trade.
Tavares was quoted as saying police were pursuing one lead that led to the jailed drug lord Jaime Gonzalez Gutierrez. The attorney himself was unavailable for comment on Saturday.
Flores, 29, was gunned down on Tuesday in broad daylight outside the La Prensa offices in the remote desert town.
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation confirmed on Friday it was helping Mexican authorities investigate the killing.
